definitions.explanation: Vegetables preserved by burying them in a fermented rice bran (nuka) bed. A traditional Japanese pickling method that produces distinctively tangy, umami-rich pickles.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{糠漬|ぬかづ}けは{絶品|ぜっぴん}だ。
examples.english: My grandmother's rice-bran pickles are superb.

examples.japanese: きゅうりの{糠漬|ぬかづ}けを{毎日|まいにち}の{食卓|しょくたく}に{出|だ}している。
examples.english: I serve cucumber rice-bran pickles at the table every day.

examples.japanese: {糠漬|ぬかづ}けを{作|つく}るには、{糠床|ぬかどこ}を{毎日|まいにち}かき{混|ま}ぜる{手間|てま}がかかる。
examples.english: Making rice-bran pickles requires the effort of stirring the bran bed every day.

notes:
USAGE:
{糠漬|ぬかづ}け is one of the most traditional forms of Japanese pickling. The key component is the {糠床|ぬかどこ} (rice bran bed), a mixture of rice bran, salt, and water that ferments over time. Common vegetables used include cucumbers, daikon, eggplant, and carrots.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糠床|ぬかどこ} (rice bran bed for pickling)
- {糠漬|ぬかづ}けを{漬|つ}ける (to make rice-bran pickles)
- {自家製|じかせい}の{糠漬|ぬかづ}け (homemade rice-bran pickles)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Maintaining a {糠床|ぬかどこ} is seen as a hallmark of a well-kept Japanese household. Some families pass down their bran beds through generations.
